serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
IVM SmartHub is an intelligent, centralized access and asset management solution designed to streamline how organizations control, track, and manage access to IVM Smart Solutions. Built for modern workplaces, government agencies, IT teams, and distributed operations, SmartHub provides secure self-service access to connected IVM solutions while maintaining full accountability through automated tracking and chain-of-custody workflows.
 
With SmartHub, organizations can reduce manual administrative tasks, improve operational visibility, and provide 24/7 controlled access to IVM Smart Solutions without requiring constant onsite support. The system helps teams manage users, permissions, access activity, inventory visibility, and asset workflows in real time, improving audit readiness and ensuring the right users have access to the right solutions when they need them.
 
Whether supporting IT service delivery, field operations, onboarding, break/fix replacement, or controlled equipment distribution, IVM SmartHub delivers a smarter, more secure, and more efficient way to manage access across the IVM Smart Solutions ecosystem.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: IVM FedRAMP Trust Center — Certification Data landing page and access instructions.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: Certification Data published as Public is served without sign-in at https://trustcenter.gov.ivminc.com/api/v1/public-documents; the newest document of a type is at https://trustcenter.gov.ivminc.com/api/v1/public-documents/latest/{type} (sdr, ocr, scg, incident, assessorexport). Other Certification Data requires sign-in. A person signs in at https://trustcenter.gov.ivminc.com/signup with their organization's Microsoft work account and submits an access request. A program uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials, one registration for each agency, and reads https://trustcenter.gov.ivminc.com/api/v1/trust-documents. To request access for a person or a program, write to trust@ivminc.com. Every route is described at https://trustcenter.gov.ivminc.com/api/v1/openapi.json.

significantChangeNotification.title: How IVM notifies necessary parties of significant changes
significantChangeNotification.description: The mechanisms available for notifying necessary parties of a significant change are: (1) direct private email, sent from the Significant Change Record to the designated contact of FedRAMP, of every agency customer IVM has on record, and of any other party IVM has agreed to notify, one message to each contact, with the recipients, channel, time and result of every send kept as a delivery record; and (2) the Significant Change register carried in this Certification Package, which lists past notices by their package-safe fields. Notices are never sent over a public channel. Replies and questions about a notice go to the Security Inbox address below.

additionalRepositories.repositoryDescription: IVM provides SmartHub's FedRAMP documentation through its Trust Center. Public Certification Data includes the service overview. Authorized agencies and assessors can request access to the Certification Package, which includes the Security Decision Record, Key Security Indicator evidence, Ongoing Certification Reports, quarterly review records, vulnerability records, significant change notifications, incident and availability information, and security policies. IVM also maintains a Secure Configuration Guide for customers. Documentation is provided in human-readable and machine-readable formats.

assessmentSummary.summary:
IVM KSI Assessment Summary
IVV-IAS-OSA
Assessors reviewed 46 KSIs against their evidence packages and SDR narratives, completing the review on 11/25/2026 based on the latest provided SDR (v. 7.0). 18 are validated, 28 are partially validated and 0 are not validated; 0 have no recorded conclusion. Mechanism verification reads 44 verified, 2 partially verified and 0 not verified, with 0 not stated. Full validation is not yet reached for most KSIs, and the shortfalls sit in implementation and review evidence rather than in the measurement mechanisms.

Reviewed 222 rules. 74 do not lie with the Cloud Service Provider and are not assessed against it. Of the 148 applicable rules, 128 are validated, 20 are partially validated and 0 are not validated. Partial outcomes on rules trace to incomplete Certification Package and Overview content, unvalidated cryptographic modules, scope and metadata coverage, Trust Center governance, and vulnerability response timeliness.

The primary gaps recorded precluding full validation are as follows, in order of priority:
• Recovery capability is not proven with certainty: checks demonstrate latest test of the database restore failed, and redeployment from infrastructure as code and application failover are untested.
• Access and credential exposure remains: phishing-resistant authentication reports as not met across some users, 2 privileged directory roles are standing rather than just-in-time, and secrets remain beyond their requirement, such as active or expired credentials, a certificate near expiry, and an exportable key.
• Configuration drift and enforcement are not fully addressed: no comparison of infrastructure as code to deployed state exists, baseline policies are Audit-only or report-only, and noncompliant resources have not been realigned with baselines.
• Integrity and traffic controls are incomplete: build-agent boot integrity fails on both scale sets and FIM is disabled on resources.
• The supply chain vendor and risk registers are pending full review and assessment.
